ops.title: internal/trust design: ship T0 + build T1 (in-process CS_OPS_BLOB leaf-OU check) in phase 1
ops.body:
Authoritative security design for internal/trust (P1c), from the fable design review
(cut/seccode/DESIGN-REVIEW.md, ~709 lines, measured on macOS 26.5.2, SIP on; supersedes the
pure-kernel-only reading). Consolidates G1 (note d9b94fb) + the SecCode decision (bfc1789).

CORE RESULT: all three candidate designs (shipped Security.framework DR, kernel-only csops,
cdhash+off-path chain) are IDENTICAL on every security row of the capability matrix. Placement
was never a security question -- it is liveness + complexity. So kernel-only ships. But there is
one asymmetry that runs AGAINST pure kernel-only and one capability that changes the fallback.

THREE TIERS (measured latencies):
  T0  kernel triple (status, category 6, teamID, identity, DER ents) ~2us; trusts amfid's
      exec-time OU==teamID enforcement (G1 PoC-confirmed).
  T1  T0 + read CS_OPS_BLOB, find the CD whose SHA256[0:20]==CS_OPS_CDHASH, resolve the CMS
      SignerInfo-designated leaf, assert leaf.Subject.OU == CD teamID == req.TeamID, plus the
      Developer ID OID markers. ~10us, NO crypto, NO I/O, NO cache. Closes R2 independently of
      the teamID string.
  T2  T1 + self-verify the CMS SignedData + chain to a pinned Apple Root CA. ~80us, zero AMFI
      dependency, but ~600-900 lines of CVE-class hand-rolled CMS parsing. NOT phase 1.

DECISION: ship T0 AND build T1 in phase 1 (not deferred). WHY T1 is phase-1, not insurance:
Security.framework's verifySignature() SILENTLY SKIPS the OU==teamID comparison when the signing
leaf has no Organizational Unit (SecCertificateCopyOrganizationalUnit==NULL -> else branch, no
error). daemonkit's old DR clause `leaf[subject.OU]="TEAM"` fails closed on such a leaf; pure T0
(reading csops teamID) does NOT -- it would serve whatever team string the CD declares. T1's
in-process OU==CD-teamID assertion turns that silent skip into a denial for ~10us. Verified
firsthand: CS_OPS_BLOB is cross-process, no root; on 1Password pid it returned the superblob with
a 9056-byte CMS wrapper and SHA256(CD)[0:20]==CS_OPS_CDHASH matched.

TWO READ-SET CORRECTIONS to DECISION §3:
  1. Require CS_VALID EXPLICITLY. The kernel gates the identity ops on CS_VALID|CS_DEBUGGED (a
     disjunction), so a successful CS_OPS_TEAMID read does NOT imply CS_VALID. Keep
     csposture.Check's CS_DEBUGGED-clear clause (csposture.go:66-68) -- it is the other half of
     that disjunction and is load-bearing, not belt-and-braces.
  2. Once T1 lands, prefer the DER entitlements from the superblob (CD-bound by construction)
     over the standalone CS_OPS_DER_ENTITLEMENTS_BLOB op.

DROP the DECISION §7 cdhash-memoized SecCodeCheckValidity fallback -- obsolete (T1 supersedes it)
and it reintroduces a measured deleted-bundle false-deny (SecCodeCopyGuestWithAttributes ->
OSStatus 100002 while the kernel reads fine on an unlink-and-replace upgrade), plus the file open,
trustd XPC, and leaked-M hazard the redesign deleted.

CRITICAL T1 IMPLEMENTATION CONSTRAINT: resolve the leaf via the CMS SignerInfo
(issuerAndSerialNumber / SKI), NEVER "the cert in the set with the right OU" -- an attacker can
stuff a decoy cert with the desired OU into the certificate set. Resolve the signer, or verify the
CMS -- never neither. Reject CS_ADHOC (0x2) and CS_LINKER_SIGNED (0x20000) in CD flags; require
hashType==SHA-256; clamp parsing to the blob's own length header, never the returned size; cap the
blob at 8 MiB and deny above; handle multi-CD superblobs (find by cdhash, not slot 0).

RESIDUALS the design must NAME (not close): (R-2 resource seal) dynamic guest validation does not
check the resource seal -- a tampered-resource copy of a signed .app passes T0/T1/T2 AND the old
Security.framework verifier. EMPTY for daemonkit's Go single-file-Mach-O fleet; FATAL for the
Electron/CEF fixed apps DESIGN G3 contemplates. The allow-jit/allow-unsigned-executable-memory
escape hatch (DESIGN §11) is not a bounded relaxation -- it is the SIGNATURE of a peer this
mechanism cannot authenticate; document as such. (Rollback) Requirement has no version floor, so
every old signed build with identifier X is a valid peer forever; name it as a DESIGN §12 open
question (MinVersion via the version package, or an n-element cdhash allowlist via artifact).
(SigningIdentifier) team-scoped namespace, not cert-bound; uniqueness is the consumer's obligation.
(fd delegation) post-admission handoff is not re-judged; AllowsHandoff is a sanctioned instance;
per-message audit-token re-verification (now ~2us, affordable) closes the exec shape but not fd
delegation.

NEW/AMENDED GATES: G5 re-run the 3-arm team-forgery trial per macOS major (only evidence for the
amfid invariant). G6 regression test: a CS_DEBUGGED peer is denied. G7 per-consumer-fixture assert
the signing leaf HAS an OU and it equals the CD teamID (catches the silent skip). G2 extend: assert
CS_OPS_BLOB's CD hashes to CS_OPS_CDHASH and the CMS slot is non-empty. G3 extend: record per
consumer whether it has a resource envelope at all.

TWO DECISION.md CORRECTIONS: "nothing for revocation to defend" is wrong for the stolen-key case
(the drop-query-time-revocation conclusion survives via the exec gate, not because there's nothing
to defend); and `defaultDeveloperIDLWCR` cited in DECISION §2 could not be corroborated anywhere --
strike it rather than inherit it into DESIGN.md.
